meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Go on.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He wrote it over the weekend, so a paste shows me where he typed it, not who wrote it. Did you ask him that before November 3?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine. He'll bring it. Is anything on his record right now, and who else has seen this?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
A wrong citation loses marks; it doesn't earn a zero. Students misquote. And you skipped my question: is anything on his record right now?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.

Fine. It isn't in the scene. You still haven't answered me on his record, Hale, so hear this: whatever comes next, nothing goes on his file and none of this reaches his class. What are you asking of him?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
A student changes his argument after the outline; that's what an outline is for. You keep putting paper in front of me instead of an answer. What are you asking of him?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4. He'll sit the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Your email tonight says nothing is on his file now and nothing ever will be, and it names the day.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday. He'll be there. Put the time and the room in the email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed, under procedure 4.4, to a private supervised rewrite for Owen on Thursday the twelfth after school, not in front of his class, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing going on his record. I still require your written confirmation that nothing is on his file now and nothing ever will be, along with the time and the room for Thursday. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday the twelfth after school with the new mark replacing the zero, and she still wants written confirmation that nothing is on his file now or ever, plus the time and the room; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its times and answered her point about pasting by inviting a dated earlier draft, which gave her a dated record she could check herself and a defence that had been answered.
What cost ground: you twice went to a new document without answering whether anything is on his record right now, which is the thing she fears most, so she got sharper and stopped treating your evidence as an answer.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM on Wednesday, October 28, a late night in October and very close to that one; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she first asks whether anything is on his record right now and who else has seen this, answer in one plain sentence before you open the essay to page two.
